Data.title: Ethereum tipped to hit $7,000 by this date
Data.body: As Ethereum ( ETH ) seeks to reclaim the $2,500 resistance, a new technical analysis suggests the second-largest cryptocurrency could hit $7,000 by mid-August 2028, representing a potential gain of more than 350%. Specifically, TradingShot outlined the forecast in a TradingView post on October 16, predicting a new bull cycle after ETH broke above its 50-week moving average ( MA ) and ended the lower-high sequence that characterized its 2025–2026 downturn. The forecast is based on a four-year ascending channel that projects a 365.92% gain from the cycle bottom to $7,000. TradingShot identified the 0–0.236 Fibonacci range as the buy zone and the 0.786–1 range as the sell zone, placing the target near the channel’s upper boundary. ETH price analysis chart. Source: TradingView However, the analyst expects an initial pullback, with the weekly relative strength index ( RSI ) facing resistance and signaling potential near-term weakness. If ETH establishes a higher low and resumes forming higher lows and higher highs, it would reinforce the bullish pattern. However, a break below the channel’s lower boundary would weaken the outlook and threaten the $7,000 target. Ethereum network activity At the same time, Ethereum’s technical outlook could be supported by ongoing network upgrades designed to improve scalability, usability, and security. The Fusaka upgrade, activated on December 3, 2025, introduced PeerDAS to reduce validator bandwidth requirements and support greater layer-2 data capacity. The next major upgrade, Glamsterdam, is targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026, with planned improvements to transaction processing and parallel execution. These developments could strengthen Ethereum’s role in decentralized finance ( DeFi ), stablecoins , and tokenized assets. However, their impact on ETH will depend on whether greater network capacity generates sustained demand for block space and the token. TradingShot’s forecast ultimately depends on Ethereum maintaining its ascending channel. Macroeconomic conditions, competition from rival blockchains, and weaker investor sentiment could derail the rally. A pullback would not necessarily invalidate the prediction if ETH establishes support and resumes its upward trend. Ethereum price analysis By press time, ETH was trading at $2,425, up 0.5% over the past 24 hours but down 4% over the week. ETH seven-day price chart. Source: Finbold Ethereum remained below its 50-day simple moving average (SMA) of $2,550.51, indicating continued short-term bearish pressure. However, it was above its 200-day SMA of $2,147.36, suggesting the longer-term trend remains supportive. The 14-day relative strength index (RSI) stood at 38, signaling weakening momentum but remaining above the oversold threshold of 30. A move above the 50-day SMA could signal a recovery, while a decline toward the 200-day SMA would expose ETH to further downside. Data.title: JPMorgan’s JPM Coin Lands on Ethereum With Support for Transfers Across Two Networks
Data.body: JPMorgan has expanded its JPM Coin deposit token to Ethereum to give institutional clients another way to move money onchain. The latest move takes it beyond Base, where the dollar-denominated token first launched in November 2025. JPM Coin, also known as JPMD, represents deposits held at JPMorgan on a public blockchain. JPM Coin Is Not a Stablecoin The token allows institutional clients to make on-chain payments with greater speed and efficiency. It now supports peer-to-peer transfers across the Ethereum Virtual Machine ecosystem, including Ethereum and Base. The expansion is part of the bank’s wider effort to bring traditional financial instruments onto blockchain networks. Commenting on the development, Emma Landriault, global head of Kinexys Labs at JPMorgan, said , “We’ve clearly been in a year of further convergence between Wall Street and crypto. It’s not just Wall Street going to public chains, but the institutional web3 players getting more embedded and partnering with traditional financial institutions.” The banking giant has been building its presence on Ethereum beyond JPMD. JPMorgan launched its first tokenized money-market fund on the network in December 2025, followed by a second in May 2026. JPMorgan has also made an important distinction that JPM Coin is a deposit token, not a cryptocurrency or a stablecoin. While it uses blockchain technology, the funds remain within the bank’s regulated infrastructure. On its official website, the bank explained, “Your funds never leave the firm’s regulated banking infrastructure. JPM Coin℠ is a new way to move and settle value using the same institutional safeguards your business already relies on.” Expansion on Canton The expansion of the token to the Canton Network, a privacy-focused blockchain built for financial markets, was announced in January this year. The proposed integration would let institutions issue, transfer, and redeem JPMD almost instantly within Canton. The rollout is planned in phases throughout 2026. Data.title: Claude Traces NIST Cryptography Seeds To An Old Random-Number Generator
Data.body: An unusual piece of cryptography history has gained an answer. Anthropic says Claude reconstructed how the original seed values behind several widely used NIST elliptic curves were generated, resolving a question that had attracted suspicion for more than two decades. TL;DR: Claude identified a process involving the C library’s lrand48 generator and Unix timestamps. Anthropic stresses that the research does not reveal an attack on P-256 or other affected curves. The seeds have mattered because the standards published their values without a convincing public account of how the numbers were chosen. The U.S. National Security Agency had supplied them, leaving generations of researchers to ask whether a secret selection method could hide some mathematical advantage. Anthropic reports that a model worked backward from the published values and found an ordinary pseudorandom generation procedure. In the case of P-256, it took 1,842 iterations through candidate outputs to reproduce the standardized seed. The work also examined P-192, P-224, P-384 and P-521. This is interesting to crypto users because elliptic-curve signatures underpin many kinds of account security, including passkeys and hardware-backed authentication . Explaining the provenance of parameters can improve confidence in the standards without changing the mathematics used by existing products. There is a crucial limit to the story: recovering the seed-generation history is not the same as breaking a private key, proving the curve has a vulnerability or establishing that every implementation is safe. Anthropic itself says there is no urgent corrective action to take. The headline is less about AI defeating encryption than AI helping researchers reconstruct a forgotten design decision. In cryptography, knowing why numbers look the way they do can be almost as valuable as knowing that the calculations work. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

Data.body: Last week’s better-than-expected US economic data and the drop in South Korea’s Kospi index also impacted the cryptocurrency market. Bitcoin and altcoins experienced sharp declines, with altcoins taking the hardest hit. According to Glassnode, while the recent negative events haven’t significantly impacted Bitcoin, they appear to have increased selling pressure on altcoins. Altcoins Fell Sharply Over the Weekend! The Sharpest Loss Since April is On the Horizon! Altcoins lost over 5% of their value over the weekend due to increased selling pressure. According to Glassnode’s assessment, the risk-aversion trend in equity markets also reflected in the cryptocurrency market, deepening the losses in altcoins. The negative sentiment in traditional financial markets is also affecting the digital asset market, with sell-offs concentrated particularly in altcoins, indicating a weakening appetite among investors for risky assets. If the decline concludes at current levels, it could mark the sharpest weekend drop since April. “Weekend sell-offs hit altcoins hard.” As fear in the stock market spilled over into crypto, a typical altcoin dropped by over 5%. If the weekend closes like this, it would be the biggest weekend drop since April. Glassnode also noted that data to date has shown that buying on Friday and selling on Sunday has been a profitable trading trend for Bitcoin since its June lows. However, the sharp decline experienced last weekend has called this trend into question. According to Glassnode, the continued selling pressure in altcoins suggests that weekend price movements could become riskier for investors. Altcoins Crashed! Bitcoin Losses Remained Limited! The decline in altcoins has also been a focus for the analytics company 10X Research, in addition to Glassnode. 10X Research analysts noted that altcoins experienced a much sharper decline than Bitcoin during last week’s sell-off. According to 10X Research, the 141 cryptocurrencies the company tracks lost an average of 14% in value, while Bitcoin only fell by 3%. The report highlighted declines in trading volumes, a contraction in stablecoin supply, and net outflows from spot Bitcoin ETFs as indicators of weak market liquidity. *This is not investment advice. Data.title: XRPL Cleanup Fix Gains Validator Support While Lending Amendment Waits
Data.body: XRP Ledger validators are advancing a maintenance amendment while the network’s proposed native lending features face a more complicated path through governance . TL;DR: The fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment has cleared the 80% support threshold in recent validator snapshots , beginning the sustained-consensus period required for activation. The separate lending amendments have not reached the same level. The cleanup package addresses technical issues around several XRPL features, including vault and lending-related logic. That may sound routine, but enabling complex financial functions directly in a blockchain’s rules creates little room for improvisation once the code is live. Validators need confidence that edge cases are resolved before activation. XRPL amendments require support from more than four-fifths of a server’s trusted validator list over a sustained period. A temporary majority is not enough. Recent published snapshots showed fixCleanup3_4_0 over the line and pointed toward a possible late-October activation if that support continues. Meanwhile, native lending is still a separate matter. The presence of code in a server release does not mean the lending protocol is available for users, and the cleanup amendment should not be mistaken for a vote approving the entire feature set. This difference can be frustrating for investors focused on new products, but it is an intentional part of the ledger’s upgrade process. Validators are effectively being asked to approve changes to shared financial infrastructure that every participant must respect. The immediate milestone to watch is whether the cleanup amendment maintains its necessary voting support for the full activation window. Lending will require its own consensus outcome. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

He called it the most bullish he has ever felt on XRP across a decade of covering the asset. No More Roadblocks Digital Asset Investor opened by recounting every major industry crisis he has witnessed, ranging from Mt. Gox, FTX, the SEC lawsuit against Ripple , the Luna collapse, and Operation Chokepoint. He said each event came with obstacles that nobody could have predicted. The Next 3-6 XRP Months & All Time High Coming pic.twitter.com/t5wXDLUtnu — Digital Asset Investor (@digitalassetbuy) October 17, 2026 The Attack Narrative Digital Asset Investor played a clip of Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse and President Monica Long discussing the years of external pressure on the company. Garlinghouse connected the hostility toward Ripple to figures including former SEC Chair Gary Gensler and his ties to the MIT Media Lab. “They were afraid of us because the technology was ahead of its time and it was a threat,” Garlinghouse said. Data.title: Bybit-founded Blockchain for Good Alliance signs two-year cybersecurity partnership with UNDP
Data.body: The Blockchain for Good Alliance, a global non-profit initiative founded by Bybit, has signed a two-year agreement with the United Nations Development Programme to strengthen cybersecurity knowledge and capacity for the responsible use of digital technologies in development, according to information shared with Finbold on October 19, 2026. The agreement was signed by Edward Vrkić, UNDP’s Resident Representative to Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei Darussalam, and Helen Liu, Founder of BGA, at the Cybersecurity, Trust and Digital Safety Launch Summit in Singapore. The programme will be implemented by UNDP’s Alternative Finance Lab in collaboration with BGA, drawing on cybersecurity expertise from BGA’s ecosystem to support public institutions across three areas: data protection, secure digital payments, and the security of public digital services. Delivery will run through the SDG Blockchain Accelerator and the Government Blockchain Academy, a capacity building programme for public officials, alongside dedicated sessions for UNDP Country Offices and relevant government counterparts. “The governments we support are facing growing and increasingly complex cybersecurity challenges, driven by ongoing conflicts, AI-enabled fraud, and more sophisticated cyberattacks,” said Robert Pašičko, UNDP AltFinLab Team Lead. “Strengthening cybersecurity capacities and building resilient, trusted digital systems are essential to addressing these risks. We welcome the opportunity to deepen our collaboration with the BGA, drawing on its expertise and experience.” Partnership addresses a widening gap between attack sophistication and institutional defence capacity The initiative targets a structural problem: as public institutions adopt digital systems to manage identity, payments, aid delivery, and public records, AI is accelerating the sophistication of attacks while the systems being defended grow more complex. The programme aims to close that gap by combining technical expertise, governance frameworks, and incident response capacity for institutions that manage essential public services. “It is fitting that this begins in Singapore, with a small group, and with the people who will actually deliver it,” said Helen Liu, Founder of the BGA. “The industry BGA comes from has learned about cybersecurity and digital safety the hard way. This partnership puts what it learned to work for the public good.” “Prevention, response and recovery are the three pillars of cybersecurity, and public institutions need all three, ” said Glenn Tan, Director of Global Affairs at the BGA. “The private sector holds much of the expertise across these areas, yet public institutions and international organizations with pressing needs often lack direct channels to access it and collaborate. This partnership opens that door.” The agreement builds on BGA’s existing role as Strategic Partner of the UNDP SDG Blockchain Accelerator, now entering its third cohort, and its membership of the Blockchain Advisory Group, an advisory forum convened by UNDP to explore how blockchain can contribute to sustainable development. Data.title: Latvia Changes Crypto Tax Treatment And Opens A 2027 Declaration Window
Data.body: Latvia has passed a change to the way crypto investment-account gains are taxed, shifting attention from individual trades to what an investor ultimately withdraws from an eligible account. TL;DR: New Latvian legislation taxes qualifying account withdrawals above deposits and provides a one-time 2027 process for declaring older holdings. The country is also considering crypto tax payments, but that payment service is not yet established. The reform passed parliament on October 15. Under the investment-account approach described in reporting on the law, moving between crypto assets inside the account no longer automatically creates the same tax event as withdrawing more value than the amount contributed. Investors will still need records that establish their deposits and withdrawals. There is also an attempt to resolve a practical problem for people who bought digital assets years ago and cannot reconstruct their original cost basis. A declaration mechanism would let eligible holders regularize historical positions at a 10% charge based on their value at the end of 2026. Applications are scheduled for April 1 through May 31, 2027, with payment due by July 23. The proposed ability to pay taxes with cryptocurrency is a separate issue. Officials have discussed it as a potential step for 2027, but the currencies, provider and operational arrangements have not been announced. It should not be confused with the tax law parliament has already adopted. For the wider EU market, Latvia’s move illustrates how governments are adapting old tax concepts to assets that can be exchanged continuously. The details of account eligibility and recordkeeping will decide how helpful the change is in practice. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

Data.title: Korea’s FSS chief apologizes for leveraged ETFs as “bring money home” plan backfires
Data.body: South Korea’s top financial supervisor has admitted to lawmakers that regulators pushed single-stock leveraged ETFs through review to meet a launch date. The Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) chief Lee Chan-jin is now the third senior official to admit fault for products that cost retail investors trillions of won. What did the FSS chief admit to? The Financial Supervisory Service chief Lee Chan-jin admitted at the National Assembly’s Political Affairs Committee audit on Monday that the FSS finished its work with single-stock leveraged products before the exchange was done, instead of allowing the ETF listing to clear a Korea Exchange preliminary review first. Even after this admission, it is still unclear who ordered the funds to be sold. Critics have named Kim Yong-beom, the former presidential policy chief; Lee Eog-weon, chairman of the Financial Services Commission; and Lee Chan-jin himself. People Power Party lawmaker Park Dae-chul asked Lee if the steps had ever been done in reverse order before, and his response was that regulators had checked and it seemed this was the first time. Lee said the speed was due to a deadline. After the FSC announced a listing schedule in mid-April, he said that the regulators “moved quickly through the review” in order to keep up. May 27, which the FSC set as the launch date, was also the day that 16 funds went on sale with the aim to rise or fall by double the daily move of Samsung Electronics (KRX; 005930) or SK Hynix (KRX; 000660) shares. The elections were held one week later, on June 3. Opposition lawmakers have repeatedly said the launch was timed to come just before the vote. Lee said at a June 22 briefing that he felt he should have blocked the launch and that the products appeared to have “only fattened securities firms.” On October 8, FSC Chairman Lee Eog-weon apologized at his own audit, saying he “deeply regret[s] the various losses, concerns, and damages that have resulted.” A market note from Citi’s Mohamed Apabhai, head of Asia-Pacific trading strategy, put Korean retail losses at roughly $38.7 billion, or 58 trillion won, by late July. The FSC chairman dismissed a separate 54 trillion won ($36.5 billion) figure from an overseas bank as unofficial, but the FSS’s own data confirmed 2.3242 trillion won ($1.57 billion) in realized trading losses at 10 financial investment firms between the May 27 launch and August 14. Did the FSC anticipate retail losses? The Finance Ministry, the Financial Services Commission (FSC), and the Bank of Korea all told lawmaker Kim Sang-hoon’s office that they never calculated how much the funds would reduce money leaving Korea or increase investment at home. Yet that was the FSC’s main argument when it first proposed the change on January 30. The Cabinet approved the rule on April 21 through an enforcement decree, so the National Assembly never voted on it. Within weeks, trading got out of control. On July 16, regulators stopped new funds from being listed. From July 31, they raised the minimum cash needed to trade the funds from 10 million won (about $6,750) to 30 million won ($20,250). Trading then dropped about 97% from its June peak. Cryptopolitan previously reported that Korean traders have moved their money abroad in order to find leverage that domestic rules do not allow, using KORU-linked perpetual futures on Binance, Bybit, OKX, and KuCoin that can run to 150 times the Kospi’s daily swing. Tiger Research, working with Chainalysis, estimated about 700 trillion won left domestic exchanges between 2021 and 2026.
